ScanRate.description:
The percentage of the configured read capacity units to use by the AWS Glue crawler. Read capacity units is a term defined by DynamoDB, and is a numeric value that acts as rate limiter for the number of reads that can be performed on that table per second.

The valid values are null or a value between 0.1 to 1.5. A null value is used when user does not provide a value, and defaults to 0.5 of the configured Read Capacity Unit (for provisioned tables), or 0.25 of the max configured Read Capacity Unit (for tables using on-demand mode).

DeleteBehavior.description: The deletion behavior when the crawler finds a deleted object. A value of LOG specifies that if a table or partition is found to no longer exist, do not delete it, only log that it was found to no longer exist. A value of DEPRECATE_IN_DATABASE specifies that if a table has been found to no longer exist, to add a property to the table that says 'DEPRECATED' and includes a timestamp with the time of deprecation.

UpdateBehavior.description: The update behavior when the crawler finds a changed schema. A value of LOG specifies that if a table or a partition already exists, and a change is detected, do not update it, only log that a change was detected. Add new tables and new partitions (including on existing tables). A value of UPDATE_IN_DATABASE specifies that if a table or partition already exists, and a change is detected, update it. Add new tables and partitions.

Description.description: A description of the schema. If description is not provided, there will not be any default value for this.

InitialSchemaVersionId.description: Represents the version ID associated with the initial schema version.

SchemaDefinition.description: Definition for the initial schema version in plain-text.

Tags.description: List of tags to tag the schema

Connections.description: A list of connection names used by the session.

Name.description: Specifies the name of the SessionCommand. Can be 'glueetl' or 'gluestreaming'.

PythonVersion.description: Specifies the Python version. The Python version indicates the version supported for jobs of type Spark.

Key.description: The key name of the tag.

Arn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the session.

CreatedOn.description: The time and date when the session was created.

DefaultArguments.description: A map array of key-value pairs. Max is 75 pairs.

GlueVersion.description: The Glue version determines the versions of Apache Spark and Python that Glue supports. The GlueVersion must be greater than 2.0.

IdleTimeout.description: The number of minutes when idle before session times out. Default is the value of Timeout.

MaxCapacity.description: The number of Glue data processing units (DPUs) that can be allocated when the job runs.

NumberOfWorkers.description: The number of workers of a defined WorkerType to use for the session.

Progress.description: The code execution progress of the session.

SecurityConfiguration.description: The name of the SecurityConfiguration structure to be used with the session.

Tags.description: The tags belonging to the session.

Timeout.description: The number of minutes before session times out.

WorkerType.description: The type of predefined worker that is allocated when a session runs.

Type.description: The data type of the Column.

MetadataOperation.description: A required metadata operation. Can only be set to CREATE.

Version.description: The table version of the Iceberg table. Defaults to 2.

Location.description: The location of the Iceberg table.

PartitionSpec.description: The partition spec for the Iceberg table.

Properties.description: The properties for the Iceberg table.

Schema.description: The schema for the Iceberg table.

WriteOrder.description: The write order for the Iceberg table.

IcebergInput.description: Specifies an IcebergInput structure that defines an Apache Iceberg metadata table.

SortOrder.description: Indicates that the column is sorted in ascending order (==1), or in descending order (==0).

RegistryName.description: The name of the schema registry that contains the schema.

SchemaArn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the schema. One of SchemaArn or SchemaName has to be provided.

SchemaName.description: The name of the schema. One of SchemaArn or SchemaName has to be provided.

SchemaId.description: A structure that contains schema identity fields. Either this or the SchemaVersionId has to be provided.

SchemaVersionId.description: The unique ID assigned to a version of the schema. Either this or the SchemaId has to be provided.

SchemaVersionNumber.description: The version number of the schema.

Parameters.description: These key-value pairs define initialization parameters for the SerDe.

SerializationLibrary.description: Usually the class that implements the SerDe. An example is org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.columnar.ColumnarSerDe.

SkewedColumnNames.description: A list of names of columns that contain skewed values.

SkewedColumnValueLocationMaps.description: A mapping of skewed values to the columns that contain them.

SkewedColumnValues.description: A list of names of columns that contain skewed values.

BucketColumns.description: A list of reducer grouping columns, clustering columns, and bucketing columns in the table.

Columns.description: A list of the Columns in the table.

Compressed.description: True if the data in the table is compressed, or False if not.

InputFormat.description: The input format: SequenceFileInputFormat (binary), or TextInputFormat, or a custom format.

Location.description: The physical location of the table. By default, this takes the form of the warehouse location, followed by the database location in the warehouse, followed by the table name.

NumberOfBuckets.description: Must be specified if the table contains any dimension columns.

OutputFormat.description: The output format: SequenceFileOutputFormat (binary), or IgnoreKeyTextOutputFormat, or a custom format.

Parameters.description: The user-supplied properties in key-value form.

SchemaReference.description: An object that references a schema stored in the AWS Glue Schema Registry.

SkewedInfo.description: The information about values that appear frequently in a column (skewed values).

SortColumns.description: A list specifying the sort order of each bucket in the table.

StoredAsSubDirectories.description: True if the table data is stored in subdirectories, or False if not.

CatalogId.description: The ID of the Data Catalog in which the table resides.

DatabaseName.description: The name of the catalog database that contains the target table.

Name.description: The name of the target table.

Owner.description: The table owner. Included for Apache Hive compatibility. Not used in the normal course of AWS Glue operations.

Parameters.description: These key-value pairs define properties associated with the table.

PartitionKeys.description: A list of columns by which the table is partitioned. Only primitive types are supported as partition keys.

Retention.description: The retention time for this table.

StorageDescriptor.description: A storage descriptor containing information about the physical storage of this table.

TableType.description: The type of this table. AWS Glue will create tables with the EXTERNAL_TABLE type. Other services, such as Athena, may create tables with additional table types.

TargetTable.description: A TableIdentifier structure that describes a target table for resource linking.

ViewDefinition.description: The view definition for the table.

ViewExpandedText.description: Included for Apache Hive compatibility. Not used in the normal course of AWS Glue operations.

ViewOriginalText.description: Included for Apache Hive compatibility. Not used in the normal course of AWS Glue operations.

IsProtected.description: Indicates whether the view is protected.

Dialect.description: The dialect of the view representation.

ViewExpandedText.description: The expanded text of the view.

ViewOriginalText.description: The original text of the view.

CatalogId.description: The ID of the Data Catalog in which to create the Table.

DatabaseName.description: The name of the database where the table metadata resides. For Hive compatibility, this must be all lowercase.

Name.description: The table name. For Hive compatibility, this is folded to lowercase when it is stored.

OpenTableFormatInput.description: Specifies an OpenTableFormatInput structure when creating an open format table.

TableInput.description: A structure used to define a table.

IcebergConfiguration.description: The configuration for an Iceberg compaction optimizer.

DeleteFileThreshold.description: The minimum number of deletes in a data file to make it eligible for compaction.

MinInputFiles.description: The minimum number of input files before compaction is triggered.

Strategy.description: The compaction strategy to use. Valid values are binpack, sort, and z-order.

Location.description: Specifies a directory in which to look for orphan files (defaults to the table's location). You may choose a sub-directory rather than the top-level table location.

OrphanFileRetentionPeriodInDays.description: The specific number of days you want to keep the orphan files.

IcebergConfiguration.description: The IcebergConfiguration property helps optimize your Iceberg tables in AWS Glue by allowing you to specify format-specific settings that control how data is stored, compressed, and managed.
The configuration for an Iceberg snapshot retention optimizer.

CompactionConfiguration.description: The configuration for a compaction optimizer. This configuration defines how data files in your table will be compacted to improve query performance and reduce storage costs.

Enabled.description: Whether the table optimization is enabled.

OrphanFileDeletionConfiguration.description: OrphanFileDeletionConfiguration is a property that can be included within the TableOptimizer resource. It controls the automatic deletion of orphaned files - files that are not tracked by the table metadata, and older than the configured age limit.

RetentionConfiguration.description: The configuration for a snapshot retention optimizer for Apache Iceberg tables.

RoleArn.description: A role passed by the caller which gives the service permission to update the resources associated with the optimizer on the caller's behalf.

VpcConfiguration.description: An object that describes the VPC configuration for a table optimizer. This configuration is necessary to perform optimization on tables that are in a customer VPC.

GlueConnectionName.description: The name of the AWS Glue connection used for the VPC for the table optimizer.

CatalogId.description: The catalog ID of the table

DatabaseName.description: The name of the database. For Hive compatibility, this is folded to lowercase when it is stored.

TableName.description: The table name. For Hive compatibility, this must be entirely lowercase.

TableOptimizerConfiguration.description: Specifies configuration details of a table optimizer.

Arguments.description: The job arguments used when this trigger fires. For this job run, they replace the default arguments set in the job definition itself.

CrawlerName.description: The name of the crawler to be used with this action.

JobName.description: The name of a job to be executed.

NotificationProperty.description: Specifies configuration properties of a job run notification.

SecurityConfiguration.description: The name of the SecurityConfiguration structure to be used with this action.

Timeout.description: The JobRun timeout in minutes. This is the maximum time that a job run can consume resources before it is terminated and enters TIMEOUT status. The default is 2,880 minutes (48 hours). This overrides the timeout value set in the parent job.

CrawlState.description: The state of the crawler to which this condition applies.

CrawlerName.description: The name of the crawler to which this condition applies.

JobName.description: The name of the job whose JobRuns this condition applies to, and on which this trigger waits.

State.description: The condition state. Currently, the values supported are SUCCEEDED, STOPPED, TIMEOUT, and FAILED.

BatchSize.description: Number of events that must be received from Amazon EventBridge before EventBridge event trigger fires.

BatchWindow.description: Window of time in seconds after which EventBridge event trigger fires. Window starts when first event is received.

NotifyDelayAfter.description: After a job run starts, the number of minutes to wait before sending a job run delay notification

Conditions.description: A list of the conditions that determine when the trigger will fire.

Logical.description: An optional field if only one condition is listed. If multiple conditions are listed, then this field is required.

Actions.description: The actions initiated by this trigger.

EventBatchingCondition.description: Batch condition that must be met (specified number of events received or batch time window expired) before EventBridge event trigger fires.

Predicate.description: The predicate of this trigger, which defines when it will fire.

Schedule.description: A cron expression used to specify the schedule.

StartOnCreation.description: Set to true to start SCHEDULED and CONDITIONAL triggers when created. True is not supported for ON_DEMAND triggers.

Tags.description: The tags to use with this trigger.

Type.description: The type of trigger that this is.

WorkflowName.description: The name of the workflow associated with the trigger.

Key.description: A key to identify the tag.

Value.description: Corresponding tag value for the key.

Configuration.description: UsageProfile configuration for supported service ex: (Jobs, Sessions).

Tags.description: The tags to be applied to this UsageProfiles.

Uri.description: The URI for accessing the resource.

Arn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the user-defined function.

ClassName.description: The Java class that contains the function code.

DatabaseName.description: The name of the catalog database in which the function is located.

ResourceUris.description: The resource URIs for the function.

DefaultRunProperties.description: A collection of properties to be used as part of each execution of the workflow

MaxConcurrentRuns.description: You can use this parameter to prevent unwanted multiple updates to data, to control costs, or in some cases, to prevent exceeding the maximum number of concurrent runs of any of the component jobs. If you leave this parameter blank, there is no limit to the number of concurrent workflow runs.
